key_insight: Interference between light’s electric and magnetic dipole interactions can generate spin and charge photocurrents in centrosymmetric crystals without breaking inversion symmetry.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism could expand photonic and optoelectronic functionality in centrosymmetric materials such as cubic silicon and SrTiO3, although AI methods and solar-cell performance are not demonstrated.
method: Develop a unified microscopic theory of electric–magnetic dipole interference.
Combine symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations.
Separate shift-like and injection-like currents and classify symmetry and polarization dependence.
evidence_signal: The theoretical analysis and calculations predict responses that scale linearly with light intensity and are roughly 10⁻³–10⁻² times conventional non-centrosymmetric responses, yet are described as experimentally accessible.
watch_item: The abstract reports no experimental validation; weak signals may complicate detection and practical device implementation.
paper_title: Spin and Charge Photocurrents from Electric-Magnetic Dipole Interference in Centrosymmetric Crystals
